facts.text: Bridesburg was named after Joseph Kirkbride, who owned land and ran a ferry over Frankford Creek, and the legislature granted him a bridge toll right in 1811.
Bridesburg’s first school, the historic Bridesburg School, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places before its demolition in the late 2000s.
The area once housed a Dow Chemical Company phenol plant, now part of the AdvanSix complex, reflecting its industrial past.
The local history collection at the Bridesburg Historical Society spans 1812‑2012, preserving photographs, newsletters, and even WWII letters.
Bridesburg’s boundaries follow the original course of Frankford Creek to the south and west and the Delaware River to the southeast, defining its historic shape.
